items.headline: FMRB executive order T-minus-3 days: sixth witness (FCC PSHSB Chief) added; House Energy and Commerce joins requesting cohort; amicus coalition grows to twelve organizations
items.diff_narrative: Yesterday the witness slate firmed to five (Locascio plus ODNI cyber lead plus NSA Cyber plus MSTIC plus CISA Director), ACLU plus Center for Democracy and Technology filed a joint Monday amicus joining the existing eight-organization coalition pressing State Farm reasoned-decision-record plus 60-day DPA Section 708 public-comment window, and OSTP confirmed no signing window before May 22. Today enters the three-business-day window before the May 15 14:00 EDT classified threshold briefing. Senator Warner's office confirms a sixth witness — the Federal Communications Commission Public Safety and Homeland Security Bureau Chief — joining Locascio plus ODNI plus NSA Cyber plus MSTIC plus CISA. The House Energy and Commerce Subcommittee on Communications and Technology Chair sends a Tuesday-morning joint letter to OSTP requesting any signed executive order include a parallel 30-day House Energy and Commerce technical review window mirroring the Senate cyber-subcommittee classified-briefing protocol. Brennan Center for Justice plus Stanford Center for Internet and Society file a joint Tuesday amicus joining the existing twelve-organization coalition (now also including two regional bar associations and two civil-society policy shops), narrowing focus to the State Farm reasoned-decision-record requirement plus a paired sixty-day DPA Section 708 public-comment window aligned to the AISI cyber-evaluation reciprocity 120-day placement window. OSTP issues a Tuesday-afternoon press-pool note holding the no-signing-before-May-22 line.

items.headline: Indo-Pacific reciprocity perimeter reaches eleven jurisdictions with Thailand; first Latin American observers (Chile, Mexico) confirm cross-hemispheric extension
items.diff_narrative: Yesterday the cohort lifted to ten named candidates after Indonesia BSSN plus Kominfo entered as formal observers with a 150-day consultation window targeting Q4 2026 mirror-signature, and Vietnam MIC confirmed Track II observer entry parallel to the Sunday Taiwan NICS announcement. Today Thailand's National Cyber Security Agency plus the Ministry of Digital Economy and Society jointly publish a Tuesday entry note as formal observers with a 180-day consultation window targeting Q1 2027 mirror signature, lifting the cohort to eleven named candidates (Singapore, Japan, South Korea, New Zealand formally; Canada, Australia, India, Taiwan, Indonesia, Vietnam, Thailand as observers) plus the originating UK and EU. The first cross-hemispheric extension confirms: Chile's National Cybersecurity Coordination Office separately announces exploratory observer status citing its February 2026 national AI strategy and the OECD GENAI working group seat, with the Mexican Federal Institute of Telecommunications signaling parallel exploratory track entry. Mistral plus Anthropic plus OpenAI plus Google DeepMind reaffirm cohort participation; the operational threshold remains Mythos-class plus GPT-5.5-class capability. The US recognition gap is now a full Tuesday wider than the Monday baseline.

items.headline: Cerebras CBRS Tuesday intraday extension to $197.10 high; Morgan Stanley adds best-ideas-list; call-skew widens to 4.1x since IPO debut

Options trade at a 4.1x call-skew at 14:00 EDT (approximately 61,400 calls vs 14,950 puts) — the widest call-skew since the IPO debut session. The cohort's institutional-buyside narrative now treats the second-trading-week Monday gap-up as the structural inflection rather than a one-day continuation.

items.headline: Ni8mare day-twelve: post-Monday-spike taper to 4.7x baseline; Brute Ratel and Havoc added to C2 attribution; T-minus-9 business days to May 21 deadline
items.diff_narrative: Yesterday day-eleven scan dropped exposed pre-1.121.0 n8n instances to approximately 4,920 (-13.7 percent from Sunday) with US at 1,650 and India at 875 and unpatched share at 33 percent; Censys confirmed the Monday-open spike at 6.4x baseline at 09:00 UTC; Microsoft Defender plus CrowdStrike Falcon plus SentinelOne Singularity published a joint telemetry note attributing the spike to Cobalt Strike plus Sliver plus Mythic C2 frameworks. Censys reports exploitation attempts moderate from the Monday 6.4x peak to approximately 4.7x baseline at 09:00 UTC, consistent with the commodity-tier exploit-kit volume tapering after the Monday-open burst. The three defensive vendors publish a Tuesday joint follow-on telemetry note adding Brute Ratel plus Havoc to the C2-framework attribution alongside the previously-flagged Cobalt Strike plus Sliver plus Mythic; CISA refreshes the KEV catalog entry with a Tuesday-edition reminder that the May 21 federal-civilian remediation deadline now sits at T-minus-9 business days. The Trail of Bits Monday seven-CVE taxonomy is now incorporated by reference into the CISA federal-civilian operational-directive working draft per Tuesday wire reporting.

items.headline: MCP-server attack-surface gap stretches to 50x; Cisco-Astrix tenancy crosses 1,470; CrowdStrike Falcon for Agentic AI ships Tuesday public preview lifting cross-vendor visibility to 74 percent

Wiz reports Defender-for-Cloud quarantine reaches 36 percent on net-new MCP servers (vs 32 percent Monday); Cisco-Astrix tenancy crosses 1,470 (vs 1,180 Monday, +25 percent) with Akamai SkyAtlas reaching 720 tenants in parallel. items.headline: Pydantic AI CVE-2026-44892 lands as eighth agent-checkpoint-and-manifest-loader CVE, extending the taxonomy to the inference-routing tier
items.diff_narrative: Yesterday LangChain CVE-2026-44712 (CVSS 8.7 LangGraph checkpoint-deserialization) landed Monday-morning Pacific completing the agent-checkpoint-and-manifest-loader exposure pattern coverage, with Trail of Bits taxonomizing seven CVEs across the May 5-11 wave (CrewAI, Haystack, AutoGen, Semantic Kernel, LangChain, LangGraph, LiteLLM) and proposing the signed-checkpoint plus manifest-allowlist-validation common-mitigation pattern. Today a fresh agentic-AI tooling-stack CVE drops at the inference-routing tier rather than the checkpoint loader path: Pydantic AI CVE-2026-44892 (CVSS 8.4) is an authenticated server-side request forgery in the tool-result-cache validator that pivots from a connected message broker to internal cloud-metadata endpoints, mirroring the Semantic Kernel CVE-2026-44638 manifest-fetcher exposure pattern at the inference-routing tier. The Pydantic maintainer team ships v0.4.7 same-day with the patch plus a paired backport advisory for v0.3.x and v0.2.x branches the NHS England blocklist references. Trail of Bits publishes a Tuesday extended addendum updating its taxonomy from seven to eight CVEs (adding Pydantic AI to the existing seven), reaffirming the signed-checkpoint plus manifest-allowlist-validation common-mitigation pattern as the structural fix and noting the DeepMind plus Meta AI plus Anthropic Monday joint preprint reference implementations already cover the inference-routing tier through the manifest-allowlist-validation schema with no schema change required.

items.headline: Unsloth ships signed-checkpoint primitive Tuesday — first local-LLM fine-tuning stack to land the joint-preprint Sigstore-or-cosign chain; Mac Studio M4 Ultra reproduction extends accessibility to Apple Silicon tier

Today's Tuesday changelog adds a fifth refinement track plus the first production landing of the joint-preprint signed-checkpoint primitive: a kernel-fused tensor-parallel router-attention backward pass on dual-Hopper workstation tiers reporting a further 14 percent training-step time reduction versus the Monday forward-pass-only mode plus a 9 percent peak combined VRAM reduction on Llama 4 Behemoth router-only training (compounding on the Monday gain); a deterministic signature-verified checkpoint save and load path tied to the DeepMind plus Meta AI plus Anthropic Monday joint preprint Sigstore-or-cosign-compatible signature chain — making Unsloth the first local-LLM fine-tuning stack to ship the signed-checkpoint primitive ahead of the framework cohort's coordinated mid-June default-shipment target; an FP8 ONNX export path for the Nvidia Blackwell deployment cohort; and a community Claude 3.7 Haiku Mixture-of-Experts recipe at 7 percent peak combined VRAM on dual-RTX 6000 Ada. A third Hacker News reproduction lands within hours documenting the Mac Studio M4 Ultra workstation completing the Mixtral 8x22B router-only recipe through the new signed-checkpoint primitive at 13 percent peak combined VRAM, extending the commodity-and-prosumer-hardware accessibility narrative to the Apple Silicon tier.

items.headline: vLLM v0.11.3 ships signed-checkpoint loader — first open-source serving stack; throughput gap narrows to 9.4 percent; Cloudflare Infire L40S advantage tightens to 1.18x
items.diff_narrative: Yesterday vLLM v0.11.2 shipped a Monday tensor-parallel disaggregated-prefill mode for dual-H100 SXM5 plus PCIe workstation tiers, with Yotta Labs placing the shared-prefix workload at 15,920 tok/s on vLLM vs 17,720 tok/s on SGLang RadixArk v0.5.5 — the throughput gap narrowing to 11.3 percent (vs 16.7 percent Sunday); Cloudflare Infire engineering reported the L40S edge-tier gap closing to a 1.25x Infire advantage (vs 1.40x Sunday). Today vLLM v0.11.3 ships a Tuesday point release adding a signature-verified model-checkpoint loader compatible with the DeepMind plus Meta AI plus Anthropic Monday joint preprint reference implementation (Sigstore-or-cosign-compatible chain), making vLLM the first open-source serving stack to ship the signed-model-checkpoint primitive at the serving tier. Yotta Labs places the shared-prefix workload at approximately 16,580 tok/s on vLLM v0.11.3 (up from 15,920 tok/s Monday) versus 18,140 tok/s on SGLang RadixArk v0.5.6 — the throughput gap narrows further to 9.4 percent (vs 11.3 percent Monday). Cloudflare Infire engineering reports that the v0.11.3 signed-checkpoint loader plus the tensor-parallel disaggregated-prefill mode close the L40S edge-tier latency gap to a 1.18x Infire advantage (vs 1.25x at the v0.11.2 Monday checkpoint), with the Cloudflare-side projection that the gap closes to parity at the v0.11.4 release window targeted late-May.

items.diff_narrative: Today opens two fresh research story-threads absent yesterday's two-paper sweep (End-to-End Sovereign-Cloud Composition Verification plus Signed-Checkpoint and Manifest-Allowlist Verification).
